citation.title: Integrated scenario in JET using real-time profile control
citation.authors: Joffrin E, Crisanti F, Felton R, Litaudon X, Mazon D, Moreau D, Zabeo L, et al. (and contributors to the JET EFDA Programme)
citation.doi_or_arxiv: unknown (PII S0741-3335(03)69281-X; DOI not stated in supplied text)

topic: JET real-time diagnostics, including charge-exchange Ti and rotation, profile mapping, and feedback control for ITER-relevant scenarios
own_question: How can real-time measurements, equilibrium reconstruction and model-based controllers improve integration and reliability of ITER-relevant scenarios at JET?
actual_method_and_evidence: Overview paper. It describes upgraded real-time diagnostics. Charge exchange provides Ti(R) and rotation on 11 channels at a 50 ms source rate, versus 2 ms for ECE and other systems (Table 1). Charge-exchange processing is synchronized to neutral beams and uses five-Gaussian fitting in under 50 ms. Profiles are remapped onto the EQUINOX flux grid. Example single-discharge feedback experiments include R/LTi control by NBI and SVD/PI q-profile control. Evidence comes from example pulses. No statistical validation is given. Figures were not visually checked.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Charge-exchange ion-temperature profiles have been produced in real time at JET, at a slower source rate (about 50 ms) than ECE electron temperature (2 ms).
claim_checks.qualification: These are reported source rates, not measured end-to-end report arrival latency. The impurity species is not specified in the text. This is JET, not KSTAR.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Real-time ion-temperature-derived quantities have been used as feedback inputs for profile control, e.g. R/LTi controlled with NBI power.
claim_checks.qualification: This is an example discharge with online control. It does not involve nowcasting or estimating missing reports.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: CX Ti is reported at about 50 ms and ECE Te at 2 ms. Profile mapping and equilibrium data are delivered at 20 ms. No inter-report estimation is performed.
validation_if_relevant: Algorithms are described as tested on many pulses; EQUINOX was compared with EFIT on more than 500 discharges. Controllers are shown in individual pulses only. No held-out evaluation is reported.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim JET nowcast CX reports between arrivals.
Do not equate CX Ti here with carbon-impurity CES on KSTAR.
Do not treat the 50 ms source rate as a measured latency.
Do not use this source to claim the control benefit of our estimator.
Do not generalize to all prior work.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as background motivating why slower ion-temperature reports matter for real-time control relative to faster electron diagnostics. It is not methodologically comparable to our study.
